S.source: printed p. 980; entry 'taupcaw'; sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 't–m–aupcaw'
S.TRANSL: I can't break up the soil, it is resistant to hoeing

S.source: printed p. 980; entry 'taupdaq'; illustrates 'taupdaq'
S.FORM: haya wa fa taupdaq sa ribush
S.PHON: haja wa fa taupdaq sa ribuʃ
S.FORM: haya wa fa taupdaq sa ribush
S.PHON: haja βa ɸa taupdaq sa ribuʃ
S.TRANSL: That vine is clinging to the plant

S.source: printed p. 980; entry 'taupdaq'; sense 2; illustrates 'pa–taupdaq'
S.FORM: pa-taupdaq sa qahil a p-in-atash-an pi-suy p-in-azim pa-taupdaq
S.PHON: pataupdaq sa qahil a pinataʃan pisuj pinaðim pataupdaq

S.PHON: pataupdaq sa qahil a pinataʃan pisuj pinaðim pataupdaq

TRANSL.notes: Literal translation: Stick the written on paper put it there on the wall, stick it

S.TRANSL: Stick the paper that has been written on against the wall

S.source: printed p. 980; entry 'taupdaq'; sense 3; illustrates 'pa–taupdaq–an'
S.TRANSL: Apply a poultice to my wound

S.source: printed p. 980; entry 'taupdaq'; sense 3; illustrates 'pa–taupdaq–an'

S.PHON: nak a biktið matðuka pataupdaqan uan ɬmir
S.FORM: nak a biktiz mat-zuka, pa-taupdaq-an uan lhmir
S.PHON: nak a biktið matðuka pataupdaqan uan ɬmir
S.TRANSL: My leg is wounded (so) please apply medicine to it

S.source: printed p. 980; entry 'taupdaq'; sense 3; illustrates 'pa–taupdaq–an'
S.FORM: nak a kuskus mat-zuka, pa-taupdaq-an sa lhmir maqa niwan ma-qitan
S.PHON: nak a kuskus matðuka pataupdaqan sa ɬmir maqa niwan maqitan
S.FORM: nak a kuskus mat-zuka, pa-taupdaq-an sa lhmir maqa niwan ma-qitan
S.PHON: nak a kuskus matðuka pataupdaqan sa ɬmir maqa niβan maqitan
S.TRANSL: My leg is wounded; put medicine on it because it hasn't yet healed

S.source: printed p. 981; entry 'taupdaq' (opens on p. 980); sense 5; illustrates 'pa–taupdaq–i'
S.TRANSL: Don't cling (to me)

S.source: printed p. 981; entry 'taupdaq' (opens on p. 980); sense 6; illustrates 'taupdaq–an'
S.FORM: haya wa ribush taupdaq-an sa fa
S.PHON: haja wa ribuʃ taupdaqan sa fa
S.FORM: haya wa ribush taupdaq-an sa fa
S.PHON: haja βa ribuʃ taupdaqan sa ɸa
S.TRANSL: That plant is being entwined by a vine

S.source: printed p. 981; entry 'tauqra(h)'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'mapa–tauqra'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: of two people lying at right angles with legs crisscrossing

S.TRANSL: The two of them are crossing their legs at right angles

S.source: printed p. 981; entry 'tauqra(h)'; sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 't–m–auqra'
S.FORM: yaku ya ma-humhum t-m-auqra sa binanau'az
S.PHON: jaku ja mahumhum tmauqra sa binanauʔað
S.FORM: yaku ya ma-humhum t-m-auqra sa binanau'az
S.PHON: jaku ja mahumhum tmauqra sa binanauʔað
S.TRANSL: At night I rest my feet/ legs on my wife

S.source: printed p. 981; entry 'tauqra(h)'; sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 't–m–auqra'
S.TRANSL: You are resting your leg on your wife

S.source: printed p. 981; entry 'taus'; sense 2; illustrates 'taus–i'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: said by A to B to call C

S.TRANSL: Call him here

S.source: printed p. 981; entry 'taus'; sense 4; illustrates 't–m–aus'
S.TRANSL: That woman is beckoning me to come

S.source: printed p. 981; entry 'taus'; sense 6; illustrates 't–m–in–aus'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: but is not beckoning to me now

S.TRANSL: He beckoned to me

S.source: printed p. 981; entry 'Tausa'; illustrates 'Tausa'
S.FORM: numa tu caw a dadú k-m-alawa sa tata wa ruza zai-n "Tausa"
S.PHON: numa tu θaw a dadu kmalawa sa tata wa ruða ðain tausa
S.FORM: numa tu thaw a dadu k-m-alawa sa tata wa ruza zai-n "Tausa"
S.PHON: numa tu θaw a dadu kmalaβa sa tata βa ruða ðain tausa
S.TRANSL: Then the chief of the Thao built a boat called Tausa

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tawahi'; sense 2; illustrates 'pun–tawahi'
S.FORM: yaku tu kahiwan pun-tawahi shi'a'ailan sa lhalhuzu patsahay-in shupak
S.PHON: jaku tu kahiwan puntawahi ʃiʔaʔailan sa ɬaɬuðu patsahajin ʃupak
S.FORM: yaku tu kahiwan pun-tawahi shi'a'ailan sa lhalhuzu patsahay-in shupak
S.PHON: jaku tu kahiβan puntaβahi ʃiʔaʔailan sa ɬaɬuðu patsahajin ʃupak
S.TRANSL: I used to go fishing for tawahi (and) I would bait the fish trap by putting the shupak fruit in it

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tay'; illustrates 'tay'
S.TRANSL: The bird has feathers already

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tazaikin'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'lhuna–tazaikin'
S.TRANSL: The dogs pursued the deer, fixing on the target as it dodged and veered

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tazaikin'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'lhuna–tazaikin'
S.FORM: haya wa shput a ma-kilhim cicu mu-ririw lhuna-tazaikin, yaku iza sa k-m-acu sa i-zay a shput sh-m-u-na-maniun
S.PHON: haja wa ʃput a makiɬim θiθu muririw ɬunataðaikin jaku iða sa kmaθu sa iðaj a ʃput ʃmunamaniun
S.FORM: haya wa shput a ma-kilhim thithu mu-ririw lhuna-tazaikin, yaku iza sa k-m-athu sa i-zay a shput sh-m-u-na-maniun
S.PHON: haja βa ʃput a makiɬim θiθu muririw ɬunataðaikin jaku iða sa kmaθu sa iðaj a ʃput ʃmunamaniun
S.TRANSL: That person is looking for him, (but) came to my place by mistake, (so) I will take him to your place

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tazaikin'; sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'maku–na–tazaikin'
S.FORM: yaku k-m-an p-in-arbu a buna, numa sa nak a qumqum maku-na-tazaikin, numa kti-ktir-ak sa buna pa-kan
S.PHON: jaku kman pinarbu a buna numa sa nak a qumqum makunataðaikin numa ktiktirak sa buna pakan
S.FORM: yaku k-m-an p-in-arbu a buna, numa sa nak a qumqum maku-na-tazaikin, numa kti-ktir-ak sa buna pa-kan
S.PHON: jaku kman pinarbu a buna numa sa nak a qumqum makunataðaikin numa ktiktirak sa buna pakan
S.TRANSL: I was eating a roast sweet potato, when my grandchild made a beeline toward me, (so) I picked it apart to feed (him)

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tazaikin'; sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'shi–tazaikin'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: answer to Did someone come to visit you?

S.TRANSL: (Someone) came to visit

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tazaikin'; sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'shi–tazaikin'
S.FORM: haya wa shput shi-tazaikin, m-zai "a mu-tusi maniun a taun"
S.PHON: haja wa ʃput ʃitaðaikin mðai a mutusi maniun a taun
S.FORM: haya wa shput shi-tazaikin, m-zai "a mu-tusi maniun a taun"
S.PHON: haja βa ʃput ʃitaðaikin mðai a mutusi maniun a taun
S.TRANSL: That person came to my house and said "I will go to your (pl.) home"

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tazam'; illustrates 'tazam'
S.FORM: tazam uan i-zay a ma-dahun k-m-an
S.PHON: taðam uan iðaj a madahun kman
S.FORM: tazam uan i-zay a ma-dahun k-m-an
S.PHON: taðam uan iðaj a madahun kman
S.TRANSL: Try eating this candy

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tazam'; illustrates 'tazam'
S.TRANSL: Please try the bananas

S.source: printed p. 982; entry 'tazam'; sense 2; illustrates 'mashin–tazam'
S.FORM: kahiwan ya fariw sa aqtalha, pasay-in pashin-taza-tazam mashin-tazam
S.PHON: kahiwan ja fariw sa aqtaɬa pasajin paʃintaðataðam maʃintaðam
S.FORM: kahiwan ya fariw sa aqtalha, pasay-in pashin-taza-tazam mashin-tazam
S.PHON: kahiβan ja ɸariw sa aqtaɬa pasajin paʃintaðataðam maʃintaðam
S.TRANSL: In the days when we bought pork we used a hand balance to weigh (it)

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 3; illustrates 'pakilh–tazam'
S.TRANSL: Come on, let's try it!

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 3; illustrates 'pakilh–tazam'
S.TRANSL: Let's try to wrestle with each other

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 4; illustrates 'pashin–tazam'
S.FORM: yaku a pashin-tazam ya la-kuza tu im-bric-an
S.PHON: jaku a paʃintaðam ja lakuða tu imbriθan
S.FORM: yaku a pashin-tazam ya la-kuza tu im-brith-an
S.PHON: jaku a paʃintaðam ja lakuða tu imbriθan
S.TRANSL: I'll weigh (them to see) how heavy they are

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 5; illustrates 'pashin–tazam–i'
S.TRANSL: Please weigh this fish on the scale

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 7; illustrates 'pu–tazam'
S.FORM: mashtay k-m-alawa pu-tazam pu-say sazum, mu-lhckiz shi-na-tmaz
S.PHON: maʃtaj kmalawa putaðam pusaj saðum muɬθkið ʃinatmað
S.FORM: mashtay k-m-alawa pu-tazam pu-say sazum, mu-lhthkiz shi-na-tmaz
S.PHON: maʃtaj kmalaβa putaðam pusaj saðum muɬθkið ʃinatmað
S.TRANSL: They all worked to try to put them in the water (but) everything sank

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 7; illustrates 'pu–tazam'
S.FORM: numa sa i-zaháy tanamarutaw parhaway m-ara sa shakish k-m-alawa sa kacu pu-tazam
S.PHON: numa sa iðahaj tanamarutaw parhawaj mara sa ʃakiʃ kmalawa sa kaθu putaðam
S.FORM: numa sa i-zahay tanamarutaw parhaway m-ara sa shakish k-m-alawa sa kathu pu-tazam
S.PHON: numa sa iðahaj tanamarutaw parhaβaj mara sa ʃakiʃ kmalaβa sa kaθu putaðam
S.TRANSL: Then that Tanamarutaw youth got a camphor tree and made it into a hull to test

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 8; illustrates 'shin–tazam'
S.FORM: shin-tazam uan uhu qilha ya ma-qmin
S.PHON: ʃintaðam uan uhu qiɬa ja maqmin
S.FORM: shin-tazam uan uhu qilha ya ma-qmin
S.PHON: ʃintaðam uan uhu qiɬa ja maqmin
S.TRANSL: Please taste the wine to see if it is strong enough

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 11; illustrates 'shu–tazam'; reading 1 of 2 of 'ata (tu) shu–tazam'
S.TRANSL: Don't measure (it)!

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 11; illustrates 'shu–tazam'; reading 2 of 2 of 'ata (tu) shu–tazam'
S.TRANSL: Don't measure (it)!

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 11; illustrates 'shu–tazam'
S.FORM: shu-tazam uan uhu sa i-zahuy a kawi ya la-kuza tu quliush
S.PHON: ʃutaðam uan uhu sa iðahuj a kawi ja lakuða tu quliuʃ

S.PHON: ʃutaðam uan uhu sa iðahuj a kaβi ja lakuða tu quliuʃ
S.TRANSL: Please measure the length of that board/ piece of wood

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 15; illustrates 'tazam–ik'
S.FORM: haya pania'an tazam-ik, ma-cuaw ma-qitan kan-in
S.PHON: haja paniaʔan taðamik maθuaw maqitan kanin
S.FORM: haya pania'an tazam-ik, ma-thuaw ma-qitan kan-in
S.PHON: haja paniaʔan taðamik maθuaw maqitan kanin
S.TRANSL: I tasted those vegetables; they are very good to eat

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 16; illustrates 't–m–azam'
S.FORM: yaku t-m-azam shnir ma-qasbit ya ma-dahun
S.PHON: jaku tmaðam ʃnir maqasbit ja madahun
S.FORM: yaku t-m-azam shnir ma-qasbit ya ma-dahun
S.PHON: jaku tmaðam ʃnir maqasbit ja madahun
S.TRANSL: I'm tasting the soup to see if it is salty or sweet

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazam' (opens on p. 982); sense 17; illustrates 'u–tazam'
S.FORM: u-tazam uan ita ya tima ma-tunaw
S.PHON: utaðam uan ita ja tima matunaw
S.FORM: u-tazam uan ita ya tima ma-tunaw
S.PHON: utaðam uan ita ja tima matunaw
S.TRANSL: Let's try to see who will win

S.source: printed p. 983; entry 'tazaq'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–tazaq'

S.PHON: nak a ina mðai nak a ama maθuaw mataðaq maqaqujaʃ
S.FORM: nak a ina m-zai nak a ama ma-thuaw ma-tazaq ma-qa-quyash
S.PHON: nak a ina mðai nak a ama maθuaw mataðaq maqaqujaʃ
S.TRANSL: My mother says my father really has a talent for singing

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'tazuqus'; illustrates 'tazuqus'
S.TRANSL: My ring is gold

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'tazuqus'; sense 2; illustrates 'pu–tazuqus–an'
S.TRANSL: I'm wearing a ring

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'tdik'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–tdik'
S.TRANSL: That path is very steep

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'tdik'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–tdik'
S.FORM: haya wa caw mun-saháy ma-tdik m-undadán
S.PHON: haja wa θaw munsahaj matdik mundadan
S.FORM: haya wa thaw mun-sahay ma-tdik m-undadan
S.PHON: haja βa θaw munsahaj matdik mundadan
S.TRANSL: That person is walking horizontally on a steep slope

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'tdik'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–tdik'
S.FORM: haya wa caw mun-saháy ma-tdik mana-saya
S.PHON: haja wa θaw munsahaj matdik manasaja
S.FORM: haya wa thaw mun-sahay ma-tdik mana-saya
S.PHON: haja βa θaw munsahaj matdik manasaja
S.TRANSL: That person is walking vertically up a steep slope

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'tdik'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–tdik'
S.TRANSL: I rolled down the slope

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'tdik'; sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–tdi–tdik'
S.FORM: haya wa hudun ma-cuaw ma-tdi-tdik, ata tu un-i-utu m-undadán, a kashum-buluq
S.PHON: haja wa hudun maθuaw matditdik ata tu uniutu mundadan a kaʃumbuluq
S.FORM: haya wa hudun ma-thuaw ma-tdi-tdik, ata tu un-i-utu m-undadan, a kashum-buluq
S.PHON: haja βa hudun maθuaw matditdik ata tu uniutu mundadan a kaʃumbuluq
S.TRANSL: That mountain is very steep, don't go walking on it or you will tumble down

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'tdik'; sense 7; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'pia–tdik'

TRANSL.notes: Source note: as a roof under construction

S.TRANSL: Make it steep!

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'thokat'; sense 2; illustrates 'min–thokat'
S.FORM: numa ya ma-dumu-dumuc iza pu-say-in iza kalawá-n a min-thokat
S.PHON: numa ja madumudumuθ iða pusajin iða kalawan a minthokat
S.FORM: numa ya ma-dumu-dumuth iza pu-say-in iza kalawa-n a min-thokat
S.PHON: numa ja madumudumuθ iða pusajin iða kalaβan a minθ*kat

TRANSL.notes: Source note: with reference to mud

S.TRANSL: Then when it was nice and soft, it was made into bricks

S.source: printed p. 984; entry 'tiaz'; illustrates 'tiaz'
S.TRANSL: She is in an advanced stage of pregnancy

S.source: printed p. 985; entry 'tiaz' (opens on p. 984); sense 4; illustrates 'ki–tiaz–an'
S.TRANSL: I have chronic stomach trouble

S.source: printed p. 985; entry 'tiaz' (opens on p. 984); sense 5; illustrates 'k–m–a–tiaz–an'
S.TRANSL: I was hit in the stomach

S.source: printed p. 985; entry 'Tibatu'; illustrates 'Tibatu'
S.FORM: numa sa Tibatu k-m-alawa sa tata wa ruza zai-n "Lawian"
S.PHON: numa sa tibatu kmalawa sa tata wa ruða ðain lawian
S.FORM: numa sa Tibatu k-m-alawa sa tata wa ruza zai-n "Lawian"
S.PHON: numa sa tibatu kmalaβa sa tata βa ruða ðain laβian
S.TRANSL: Then the Shih family built a boat called Lawian

S.source: printed p. 985; entry 'tici'; sense 2; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'an–tici–an'
S.TRANSL: He caught malaria (and got) a fever and chills

S.source: printed p. 985; entry 'tici'; sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'ma–tici'
S.TRANSL: Snow is cold (to the touch)

S.source: printed p. 985; entry 'tici'; sense 3; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'matici'
S.TRANSL: This tea is cold already

S.source: printed p. 986; entry 'tici' (opens on p. 985); sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'min–tici'
S.TRANSL: The rice is getting cold

S.source: printed p. 986; entry 'tici' (opens on p. 985); sense 4; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'min–tici'
S.TRANSL: I'm getting cold

S.source: printed p. 986; entry 'tici' (opens on p. 985); sense 5; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'pash–tici'
S.TRANSL: That tea is hot-please let it cool

S.source: printed p. 986; entry 'tici' (opens on p. 985); sense 6; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'pash–tici–n'
S.FORM: numa ya p-in-in-tata iza pu-say-in iza ka-danar-an pash-tici-n, numa ya ma-tici iza tiktik-in cicu
S.PHON: numa ja pinintata iða pusajin iða kadanaran paʃtiθin numa ja matiθi iða tiktikin θiθu
S.FORM: numa ya p-in-in-tata iza pu-say-in iza ka-danar-an pash-tithi-n, numa ya ma-tithi iza tiktik-in thithu
S.PHON: numa ja pinintata iða pusajin iða kadanaran paʃtiθin numa ja matiθi iða tiktikin θiθu
S.TRANSL: Then when it was cooked it was put on a cutting board to cool off, and when it was cool it was chopped up

S.source: printed p. 986; entry 'tici' (opens on p. 985); sense 6; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'pash–tici–n'
S.FORM: numa ya malhacas iza ar-ara-n iza pu-say-in pashzamuq pash-tici-n, numa ya ma-tici iza p-utu-an iza sa i-say a sabu sa bulbul sabu-an flhush
S.PHON: numa ja maɬaθas iða araran iða pusajin paʃðamuq paʃtiθin numa ja matiθi iða putuan iða sa isaj a sabu sa bulbul sabuan fɬuʃ
S.FORM: numa ya malhathas iza ar-ara-n iza pu-say-in pashzamuq pash-tithi-n, numa ya ma-tithi iza p-utu-an iza sa i-say a sabu sa bulbul sabu-an flhush
S.PHON: numa ja maɬaθas iða araran iða pusajin paʃðamuq paʃtiθin numa ja matiθi iða putuan iða sa isaj a sabu sa bulbul sabuan ɸɬuʃ
S.TRANSL: Then when it is cooked it is fetched and put in a winnowing basket to cool, and when it is cool a covering of flhush leaves is put there to cover the bulbul

S.source: printed p. 986; entry 'tici' (opens on p. 985); sense 7; bound root marked with bars; illustrates 'pu–tici–tici–an'
S.FORM: ya ma-cuaw an-tata-n sa but, pu-tici-tici-an sa rikus ma-shimzaw, ar-ara-n sa shput, kari-n caycuy pin-lhmir, pin-tatá-n caycuy i-qilhá-n caycuy sa shnir, numa ya ma-tata mu-hiaw ma-qitan sa but
S.PHON: ja maθuaw antatan sa but putiθitiθian sa rikus maʃimðaw araran sa ʃput karin θajθuj pinɬmir pintatan θajθuj iqiɬan θajθuj sa ʃnir numa ja matata muhiaw maqitan sa but
S.FORM: ya ma-thuaw an-tata-n sa but, pu-tithi-tithi-an sa rikus ma-shimzaw, ar-ara-n sa shput, kari-n thaythuy pin-lhmir, pin-tata-n thaythuy i-qilha-n thaythuy sa shnir, numa ya ma-tata mu-hiaw ma-qitan sa but
S.PHON: ja maθuaw antatan sa but putiθitiθian sa rikus maʃimðaw araran sa ʃput karin θajθuj pinɬmir pintatan θajθuj iqiɬan θajθuj sa ʃnir numa ja matata muhiaw maqitan sa but
S.TRANSL: If you are very feverish (and) your back feels cold all over people get it-they dig it up to make into medicine (and) the ones who are feverish drink the juice so that the fever quickly improves
